terms.gloss: not know, be unacquainted with (a person or a thing); fail to recognize
evidence: Plaut. Amph. 37: illī inīquī jūs ignōrant neque tenent
Cic. Ac. 2.4: quī illum ignōrābant (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The sense “take no notice of, disregard” is rare (Lewis & Short); the usual word for that is neglegō.

terms.gloss: not know (a fact, or how to do something)
evidence: Cic. Tusc. 1.60: nec mē pudet fatērī nescīre, quod nesciam (Lewis & Short)
Ter. Eun. 4.7.29: nescīs cui maledīcās nunc virō (Lewis & Short)

phrases.latin: nisi etiam is quoque mē ignōrābit
phrases.english: unless he too is going to fail to know me

phrases.latin: nec mē pudet fatērī nescīre, quod nesciam
phrases.english: nor am I ashamed to admit that I do not know what I do not know

sources: Lewis & Short: ignoro · Lewis & Short: nescio
